title: Villa Jaguar
style: Cinematic nu-metal with jagged drop-tuned guitar riffs, syncopated half-time drums, distorted bass, and forceful low male vocals shifting between tight rhythmic verse delivery and a broad anthemic chorus. Layer bold, tense brass stabs and deep tambora patterns into the groove; open with ominous brass and hand percussion, build through clipped verses, hit a crushing chorus, drop to a sparse percussion-and-voice bridge, then return with full-band weight. Dark, urgent, documentary-like storytelling, modern punchy mix with raw vocal edges and wide cinematic low end.
lyrics:
[Intro]
La Guajira, November—dust across the wire
Villa Jaguar, engines climbing, rifles aimed higher

[Verse 1]
Fifty came in trucks through the hard eastern ground
Wayuu and outsiders, armored engines loud
M16s, AKs, a convoy at the gate
Thomas García inside as the minutes narrowed fate
Beside Punta Espada, where the new roads were planned
His team and two local leaders stood inside the land
Investigators say the target was a man, not a name
An assassination attempt wrapped in a regional blame

[Pre-Chorus]
They wore the shape of an old wound
To hide who brought the violence through

[Chorus]
Villa Jaguar—hold the names against the dust
Five lives taken, two more wounded in the rush
Fourteen down, twenty-two hurt, nine in chains
Some escaped beyond the ridges, leaving grief across the plain
Villa Jaguar—let the record stand clear:
The neighbors condemned the assault; they did not welcome fear

[Verse 2]
Three guards fell there; two workers later died
Two more security men carried wounds inside
The attackers’ toll was heavy, many came from far away
Beyond the eastern Upper Guajira, far from home that day
A compromised Wayuu leader was among the dead
A Córdoba AGC captain was taken instead
Wanted under warrants, held as the dust fell still
While survivors counted losses against the hillside’s will

[Pre-Chorus]
They tried to dress the raid as local strife
But the evidence cuts through the lie

[Chorus]
Villa Jaguar—hold the names against the dust
Five lives taken, two more wounded in the rush
Fourteen down, twenty-two hurt, nine in chains
Some escaped beyond the ridges, leaving grief across the plain
Villa Jaguar—let the record stand clear:
The neighbors condemned the assault; they did not welcome fear

[Bridge]
Around Punta Espada, leaders spoke as one
Even those who opposed the project said this was not their cause
No banner can turn a killing into justice
No borrowed grievance can make the dead belong to someone else

[Final Chorus]
Villa Jaguar—hold the names against the dust
Five lives taken, two more wounded in the rush
Fourteen down, twenty-two hurt, nine in chains
Some escaped beyond the ridges, leaving grief across the plain
Villa Jaguar—let the record stand clear:
The neighbors condemned the assault; the truth must persevere

[Outro]
La Guajira, November
Count the living
Name the dead
